```
cd $ROOT/$D || exit 98
ldd $EXE | grep "not found" && { echo "FATAL: missing libraries"; exit 97; }

( sleep $(( SEC - ${STOP_MARGIN:-300} )); echo "LSTOP = .TRUE." > STOPCAR; echo "STOPCAR written $(date)" ) &
t0=$(date +%s)
mpirun -np $SLURM_NTASKS $EXE > vasp.out 2>&1
```

### Claude (11-20 03:30)

I took "new Fe ML potential" to mean the A1 runs: VASP on-the-fly MLFF (machine-learned force field) trained from scratch on 64-atom hcp and fcc Fe, job 7286841. No DeePMD model has been trained yet; tell me if you meant a different potential.

**Timings.** Only 9 of the 40 runs finished; all ran on 32 ranks.

| run | DFT steps | s per DFT step | ms per ML step | wall | DFT calls in last 1000 steps | basis size |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hcp P0 T1300 | 106 | 41.6 | 35 | 76 min | 8 | 104 |
| hcp P200 T300 | 36 | 19.0 | 26 | 14 min | 0 | 32 |
| hcp P300 T4200 | 81 | 20.0 | 46 | 31 min | 5 | 78 |
| fcc P0 T1700 | 165 | 43.0 | 43 | 122 min | 15 | 162 |
| fcc P300 T2400 | 71 | 24.5 | 47 | 33 min | 4 | 71 |
| fcc P360 T4600 | 108 | 21.9 | 47 | 43 min | 5 | 104 |

The other three finished runs (fcc P200/300 K, fcc P360/300 K, fcc P200/2000 K... see note below) look the same: 54–58 DFT steps, 25–27 min.

- **ML step:** 26–47 ms per MD step, about 21–38 steps/s for 64 atoms. A DFT step at 500 eV and Γ takes 19–43 s, so the ML step is about 1000× faster.
- **DFT share:** only 0.7–3.3 % of the 5000 steps were DFT, but they took 90–97 % of the wall time.
- **Still learning:** most runs still call DFT 4–15 times per 1000 steps near the end, so the force field has not converged.
- **Cost grows with basis size:** this from-scratch force field is cheap because its basis is small (32–162). The smoke run that continued the old 913-config ML_AB took 0.2 s per ML step, so a combined force field will be several times slower than these numbers.

**Problems with the other 31 runs:**
1. **20 were killed for running out of memory in under 1 minute.** They died at "Preparing memory for new training data": one node hit 35 GB. This is the memory VASP reserves up front for `ML_MB = 6000` / `ML_MCONF = 4000`, landing on a node with too few granted cores. The 9 that finished used the same settings.
2. **11 hit the 6 h limit at 1,300–16,000 s per DFT step,** versus 19–43 s in the good runs. This is the same Intel `mpirun` rank-placement problem that hit R1. They managed only 0–26 MD steps.
3. **VASP cut `NSW` from 8000 to 5000** (the OUTCAR says so), so the finished runs are 5 ps, not 8 ps. I haven't found the cause yet.

**Fix:** switch `fe_a1_job.sh` to `srun --mpi=pmi2` and rerun the 31. I'd also either lower `ML_MB` / `ML_MCONF` (the basis never went above 162) or keep the 8 GB/task and let `srun` place the ranks. Both should cure the out-of-memory kills.

**R1 speed test (debug job 7315550), which you asked about last night:** neither variant converged in 25 minutes.
- **VeryFast + EDIFF 1e-5:** 25 SCF steps, energy still jumping by 3.7 eV, so it is unstable here.
- **Fast + EDIFF 1e-5 + LREAL Auto:** 75 steps, energy change still 3×10⁻³ eV.

So neither beats the converged reference (35 SCF steps on 2 nodes). The R1 slowness was rank placement, not the INCAR, so I recommend keeping the reference INCAR and just switching to `srun`/PMI2.

I updated the A1 row in `INPROGRESS.md`. Shall I fix the job scripts and resubmit the failed A1 and R1 tasks?

```
Stock VASP (`~/bin/vasp_gam`, `vasp_std`; vasp 6.6.0 built 2026-04-25, no WSDA code) is linked against oneAPI 2025.3, which provides MKL `.so.2`. `load_intel` loads 2026.1, which has MKL `.so.3`, so these binaries fail to start under it.

Working recipe (`Claude/tools/vasp_array.sh`, 2026-10-14):
- `source /groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh --force`.
- Set LD_LIBRARY_PATH explicitly to the 2025.3 `mkl`, `compiler` and `mpi/2021.17` lib dirs, plus `~/lib` (HDF5). `.bashrc` stops early in batch ("This line only runs in interactive mode"), so it never adds `~/lib`.
- Launch with Intel `mpirun -np $SLURM_NTASKS`, not `srun --mpi=pmi2`. srun ranks lost the oneAPI environment: first MKL not found, then "OFI fi_getinfo() failed".
```

### Claude (11-20 03:49)

You're right, and that was my mistake. A1 only uses VASP's on-the-fly force field to drive the MD; its frames go through SOAP/FPS selection, then get recalculated with the R1 DFT settings and become DeePMD training data. There is no combined VASP force field, so my remark that one would be slower doesn't apply.

So "the new Fe ML potential" doesn't exist yet: no DeePMD model has been trained. The useful timings are the costs of getting its training data:

- **Sampling (A1, VASP force field driving the MD):** 14–122 min per 5 ps trajectory on 32 ranks. 90–97 % of that is the 36–165 DFT calls at 19–43 s each; the force-field steps take 26–47 ms. That the sampler keeps calling DFT near the end only matters as cost.
- **Recalculation (labels for DeePMD):** for the 128-atom R1 frames, 35–45 SCF steps × about 70 s = 45–55 min per frame on 2 × 32 ranks, when the ranks are placed properly. The 64-atom A1 frames should be several times cheaper. That's an estimate; none have been run yet.
- **DeePMD training and MD speed:** nothing to report until the first model is trained on the R1 and A1 data.

Because the VASP force field is only a sampler, I can cut `ML_MB` / `ML_MCONF` freely; the basis never went above 162. That should stop the 20 out-of-memory kills without losing anything. The 11 timeouts still need the switch from Intel `mpirun` to `srun --mpi=pmi2`.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SOAP descriptors + farthest-point selection of frames, the equivalent of X. Deng's mldp steps 1-2
(asap gen_desc --fxyz F soap -c 6 -n 6 -l 6 -g 0.44; asap/select_frames.py -n N), written because asaplib 0.0.x in
/central/groups/carnegie_poc/xind/mambaforge fails with the installed dscribe (SOAP(rcut=...) -> TypeError: dscribe
renamed rcut/nmax/lmax to r_cut/n_max/l_max).

Global descriptor of a frame = the average of its atomic SOAP vectors (asap's default 'average' reducer), normalized;
FPS with Euclidean distance, starting from the frame farthest from the mean. Writes the selected 0-based indices in
selection order to OUT (and the descriptors to OUT.desc.npy).

Run with the mambaforge python (dscribe, ase):
  /central/groups/carnegie_poc/xind/mambaforge/bin/python soap_fps.py frames.xyz -n 150 -o fps-n-150.index
2026-11-19.
"""
import argparse

import numpy as np
from ase.io import read
from dscribe.descriptors import SOAP


def fps(X, n):
    d = np.linalg.norm(X - X.mean(0), axis=1)
    sel = [int(np.argmax(d))]
    dmin = np.linalg.norm(X - X[sel[0]], axis=1)
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        k = int(np.argmax(dmin)); sel.append(k)
        dmin = np.minimum(dmin, np.linalg.norm(X - X[k], axis=1))
    return np.array(sel), dmin


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('fxyz'); ap.add_argument('-n', type=int, default=150); ap.add_argument('-o', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('-c', type=float, default=6.0); ap.add_argument('--nmax', type=int, default=6)
    ap.add_argument('--lmax', type=int, default=6); ap.add_argument('-g', type=float, default=0.44)
    ap.add_argument('-j', type=int, default=1, help='dscribe n_jobs')
    a = ap.parse_args()
    frames = read(a.fxyz, ':')
    species = sorted({s for f in frames for s in f.get_chemical_symbols()})
```

```
    soap = SOAP(species=species, r_cut=a.c, n_max=a.nmax, l_max=a.lmax, sigma=a.g, periodic=True, average='inner')
```

### Claude (11-20 04:06)

Done: the DFT recalculations are running, and a DeePMD training job is queued behind them. I started no VASP ML runs and won't rerun the failed A1 sampler runs.

**Submitted**
1. **R1, old 128-atom configs (job 7336467, 139 tasks):** every old/old_b frame that hasn't finished. `fe_r1_job.sh` now uses `srun --mpi=pmi2`. The first task runs at 75 s per SCF step, the normal speed (the misplaced `mpirun` runs took 730–1420 s).
2. **R1b, 64-atom hcp/fcc frames (job 7336666, 328 tasks, 1 node each):** same DFT settings as R1, with SIGMA = k_BT of each state. Frames come from two sources:
   - **Trajectory frames (8 states):** 25 picked by SOAP + farthest-point selection from each of the 8 A1 runs that finished, after dropping the first 1 ps.
   - **Rattled frames (32 states):** 4 per state for the states with no trajectory, including all of hcp at 360 GPa and everything at 100 GPa. Each is the A1 POSCAR lattice with a 1 % random strain and random thermal displacements. The displacement size, u² = A(V)·T, is fitted to the 8 trajectories (fit within about 20 %).
3. **DeePMD iteration 00 (job 7336710, P100):** starts when both arrays end. It gathers the finished frames, keeping only those where SCF converged, the top band is empty and |F| < 30 eV/Å, with fparam = SIGMA. It then writes `input.json` using Xin's pure-Fe architecture with sel raised to 200 for 360 GPa, then trains for 600k steps, freezes, compresses, and runs `dp test`. Xin's training of the same size took 1.3 h on a V100.

**Rough cost (my estimate, not yet measured)**
- R1: about 50 min per frame on 2 nodes, about 220 node-h.
- R1b: maybe 15–20 min per frame on 1 node, about 100 node-h.
- When training starts depends on the queue: it waits for the last DFT task to finish. If that's too slow, I can train on whatever has finished at a set time.

**Next:** iteration 01. That means running DeePMD MD in LAMMPS at all 40 states, picking the frames with the largest error against DFT, recalculating them, and retraining.

### Claude (11-20 10:32)

I added 210 DFT frames of hcp vacancies and grain boundaries, covering 0, 100, 200, 300 and 350 GPa. They are submitted as job 7349073 (210 tasks), and the DeePMD training job (7336710) now includes them and waits for them to finish. The first version had 100–350 GPa; after your note I added 0 GPa before submitting. Nothing has run yet, so I can't confirm the run times or that the grain-boundary SCF converges.

**Grid:** hcp only, at those 5 pressures × T = 300 K and 0.4, 0.7 and 0.95 T_m.
- The volume at each P and T includes thermal expansion. I estimated it from the 8 finished A1 trajectories, which show about 0.01 GPa/K of thermal pressure; at 5000 K that is roughly 50 GPa.
- Atoms are displaced randomly by the thermal amount at each T, fitted to the same trajectories. Frames with any atom pair closer than 0.7 × the nearest-neighbour distance are redrawn.

| cell | atoms | frames per pressure | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vacancy (64-atom cell minus one) | 63 | 3 at each T | 60 |
| Vacancy jump, in-plane and out-of-plane: neighbour ¼, ½ and ¾ of the way to the vacancy at 300 K, and ½ at 0.7 T_m | 63 | 8 | 40 |
| Σ7 [0001] tilt boundary, two boundaries 9.7 Å apart | 52 | 2 at each T | 40 |
| Σ7, one grain rigidly slid by ¼, ½ and ¾ of the in-plane repeat, and by c/2 along the tilt axis, at 300 K | 52 | 4 | 20 |
| {10-12} twin, built as a Σ13 boundary with c/a = 1.6036 | 100 | 1 at 300 K, 2 at each higher T | 35 |
| Twin, slid by a/2 and by ¼ and ½ of the repeat along the shear direction (300 K) | 100 | 3 | 15 |

Each pressure × temperature point gets its own DFT input set, giving 80 in total.

**Things you may want to change:**
- **Twin geometry:** the twin cell forces c/a to 1.6036, the matching value closest to the 1.60 used for A1. It also removes 4 boundary atoms that sat closer than 0.8 × the nearest-neighbour distance, so it is not a perfect coherent twin.
- **Slid frames:** these are unrelaxed. Each boundary is opened along its normal by up to 0.9 Å, because otherwise atoms collide at the boundary. They give the potential sliding-type environments but are not real energy profiles for sliding.
- **k-points:** the boundary cells are long and thin, so I made the k-point mesh at least as dense as for the 64-atom bulk cells. The twin then needs 8×4×1 k-points, which makes it the most expensive cell: my estimate is about 2–3 h per frame on 2 nodes, and the job limit is 8 h.

Larger relaxed boundaries and diffusing vacancies would be sampled later with DeePMD MD, once a first model exists.

The new builder is `~/Claude/tools/fe_r1d_defects.py`, and the frames are in `.../ML/R1/def/`. I recorded the details in Part 4 of the R1 `README.md` and in a new `INPROGRESS.md` row.

```
## 2. State points and cells

### 2.1 State points

- **Primary pressure:** 330 GPa (inner-core boundary). **Secondary:** 360 GPa (centre, 364 GPa), at two temperatures.
- **Temperatures are set by the model's own melting point $T_m$** (A3), because homologous temperature controls defect populations, premelting and diffusion:
  - $T/T_m$ ≈ 0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 0.95, 0.98;
  - provisionally 4400, 5000, 5600, 6000, 6200 K if $T_m$(330 GPa) ≈ 6300 K. Published values are 5500–6400 K (Alfè 2009; Anzellini et al. 2013; Sinmyo et al. 2019) (†).
- **One liquid state** at $T_m$ + 300 K (GK η₀; the counterpart of the MgO and MgSiO₃ liquid branch).
- **Cell geometry.** Each (P, T) is NPT-equilibrated (aniso, c/a free; 50 ps) and then run in NVT at the mean cell. Estimates: V ≈ 6.85 Å³/atom, a ≈ 2.15 Å, c ≈ 3.43 Å at 330 GPa and 5500 K.
```

### Claude (11-20 11:38)

I added your iteration loop to the Fe plan as a new §3.2 in `ANELASTICITY_PLAN_FE.md`. I also submitted one extra training job, 7351391, which the loop needs before it can start.

**Why the extra job:** to "test" MD frames we can't run DFT on all of them, since a 128-atom frame takes 45–76 min. The usual way is to train 4 models that differ only in their random seed. Where they disagree on the forces, the frame is badly predicted, and only those frames go to DFT. Job 7336710 trains model 1. Job 7351391 trains models 2–4 on the same data, on three P100s at once, and starts only if 7336710 succeeds. The queued VASP jobs are unchanged.

**What §3.2 says:**
- **MD runs, in DFT-sized cells (≤ 128 atoms)** so any flagged frame can go straight to DFT:
  - perfect hcp and fcc;
  - hcp with 1 or 2 vacancies;
  - hcp basal stacking fault;
  - Σ7 tilt boundary;
  - {10-12} twin;
  - sheared copies of these at 1–3 % strain, the range of the anelastic runs.
- **Grid:** 0–350 GPa at 300 K and 0.4, 0.7 and 0.95 T_m, plus 1.05 T_m to sample premelting. Runs are 20 ps at first, doubled each iteration.
- **Sorting frames:** the spread of the 4 models' forces on the worst atom (Eq. 7) puts each frame in one of three classes (Eq. 8):

  | class | spread |
  |---|---|
  | accurate | below 0.15 eV/Å |
  | sent to DFT | 0.15–0.5 eV/Å |
  | failed (unphysical) | above 0.5 eV/Å |

  These limits are a starting guess. I'll set them once the first models exist by comparing the spread with the true DFT errors; at 6000 K they may need to be relative to the force size.
- **Each round:** up to 10 frames per cell and state, picked to avoid near-duplicates, are recomputed with DFT at the current settings. One frame per cell and state is kept out of training as a fixed test set. The 4 models are then retrained from the previous ones for 200k steps.
- **"Stable" means all three hold in the same round:**
  - at least 99 % of frames accurate and under 0.1 % failed in every cell and state;
  - the test set meets the targets: energy under 3 meV/atom, force error under 0.15 eV/Å (under 10 % near melting), stress under 1.5 GPa;
  - the test error has stopped dropping from one round to the next.
- **After that:** the final model is retrained from scratch. A last check runs MD on the 4096–8192-atom production cells (vacancies, twin, Σ7, polycrystal). Any atoms the models disagree on are cut out into small cells for one more DFT round. The validation tests (equation of state, elastic constants, melting point) and the go/no-go decision come after that.

The DFT dominates the cost of each round: up to about 1750 frames at roughly 1 node-hour each, in practice a few hundred. If more than about 300 frames are flagged, I'll cut the cap to 5 per cell and state. The MD is about 50 GPU-hours and training is about 8 P100-hours.

**Next:** I still have to write the two scripts for the loop: `fe_dp_explore.py` sets up and submits the MD runs, and `fe_dp_select.py` picks the frames and sets up their DFT runs. I'll write them while the DFT and training jobs are queued. The job is also recorded in `INPROGRESS.md` and in a new `README.md` in `.../ML/DP/00`.

### Claude (11-20 12:04)

You're right, I'd got Xin's workflow wrong. Each round runs MD with the current model, picks a diverse sample of frames, and runs DFT on that sample. Frames whose true error is too large go into training, and the rest become test data. One model is enough, so I've cancelled job 7351391, which was training the three extra models. Training job 7336710 and the queued DFT jobs are unchanged.

I rewrote §3.2 of `ANELASTICITY_PLAN_FE.md` to follow Xin's loop. Each round:
1. **MD** with the current model on the small test cells: perfect hcp and fcc, 1–2 vacancies, basal stacking fault, Σ7 tilt boundary, {10-12} twin, and sheared copies. They run at 0–350 GPa and 300 K up to 1.05 T_m. The cells stay at 128 atoms or fewer, so sampled frames go straight to DFT.
2. **Sample** frames from each run with Xin's descriptor and selection method (SOAP + FPS).
3. **DFT** on the sampled frames with the current settings.
4. **Compare** the model against DFT with `dp test` on those frames.
5. **Split by true error** (Eq. 7, as Xin's `analysis.py`). A frame is badly predicted if its energy error is above 0.012 eV/atom or its force RMSE is above 0.44 eV/Å, her cutoffs. Those frames go into training, and all the others go into a growing test set.
6. **Retrain**, starting from the previous model.

The loop stops when the badly predicted fraction is under 5 % in every cell and state, the MD is stable, and the test-set errors meet the targets and have stopped improving. A last round on the 4096–8192-atom production cells comes before the validation tests.

Two things in the plan that you may want to change:
- **Force cutoff:** a fixed 0.44 eV/Å is loose at 300 K and tight near melting, where forces are several eV/Å. I've planned to revisit it after round 01 using the error distribution at each temperature.
- **Frames per run:** 175 runs at 2–4 frames each is 350–700 DFT frames per round, about 350–700 node-hours. Cells that pass drop out of later rounds.

I'll write the tools for the loop next: one sets up the MD runs, one samples frames and sets up the DFT, and one splits frames by error.

### Claude (11-20 12:27)

I've updated §3.2 of `ANELASTICITY_PLAN_FE.md`: the cutoffs are now set each round so that only 10–20 % of the frames tested against DFT go into training.

- **How the cutoffs are set:** they sit at the 80th–90th percentile of that round's errors. A frame is added if either its energy or its force error exceeds its cutoff. Because those two sets overlap only partly, the splitting tool will lower the two cutoffs together until the combined fraction is 10–20 %.
- **Per temperature band:** the percentile is taken within each band. Otherwise the 0.95–1.05 T_m runs, which have the largest absolute errors, would take all the training slots. Xin's 0.012 eV/atom and 0.44 eV/Å stay in the plan only as a reference.
- **Run sizes:** the frames sampled per MD run and the MD lengths can now change from round to round.
- **When to stop:** with a fixed 10–20 % going to training every round, "fraction badly predicted" can no longer measure convergence. So I changed the stopping rule. The loop stops when the cutoffs themselves fall below the error targets in every cell and state: energy under 3 meV/atom, and force error under 0.15 eV/Å up to 0.7 T_m or under 10 % near melting. At that point even the worst 10–20 % are accurate enough, and adding them no longer changes the model.

Next I'll write the three loop tools; nothing new has been submitted.

```
"""SOAP descriptors + farthest-point selection of frames, the equivalent of X. Deng's mldp steps 1-2
(asap gen_desc --fxyz F soap -c 6 -n 6 -l 6 -g 0.44; asap/select_frames.py -n N), written because asaplib 0.0.x in
/central/groups/carnegie_poc/xind/mambaforge fails with the installed dscribe (SOAP(rcut=...) -> TypeError: dscribe
renamed rcut/nmax/lmax to r_cut/n_max/l_max).

Global descriptor of a frame = the average of its atomic SOAP vectors (asap's default 'average' reducer), normalized;
FPS with Euclidean distance, starting from the frame farthest from the mean. Writes the selected 0-based indices in
selection order to OUT (and the descriptors to OUT.desc.npy).

Run with the mambaforge python (dscribe, ase):
  /central/groups/carnegie_poc/xind/mambaforge/bin/python soap_fps.py frames.xyz -n 150 -o fps-n-150.index
2026-11-19.
"""
import argparse

import numpy as np
from ase.io import read
from dscribe.descriptors import SOAP


def fps(X, n):
    d = np.linalg.norm(X - X.mean(0), axis=1)
    sel = [int(np.argmax(d))]
    dmin = np.linalg.norm(X - X[sel[0]], axis=1)
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        k = int(np.argmax(dmin)); sel.append(k)
        dmin = np.minimum(dmin, np.linalg.norm(X - X[k], axis=1))
    return np.array(sel), dmin


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('fxyz'); ap.add_argument('-n', type=int, default=150); ap.add_argument('-o', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('-c', type=float, default=6.0); ap.add_argument('--nmax', type=int, default=6)
    ap.add_argument('--lmax', type=int, default=6); ap.add_argument('-g', type=float, default=0.44)
    ap.add_argument('-j', type=int, default=1, help='dscribe n_jobs')
    a = ap.parse_args()
    frames = read(a.fxyz, ':')
    species = sorted({s for f in frames for s in f.get_chemical_symbols()})
    soap = SOAP(species=species, r_cut=a.c, n_max=a.nmax, l_max=a.lmax, sigma=a.g, periodic=True, average='inner')
    X = np.array(soap.create(frames, n_jobs=a.j))
    X /= np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1)[:, None]
    np.save(a.o + '.desc.npy', X)
    sel, dmin = fps(X, a.n)
    np.savetxt(a.o, sel, fmt='%d', header=f'FPS order, 0-based; SOAP c {a.c} n {a.nmax} l {a.lmax} g {a.g}; {len(frames)} frames')
    print(f"{len(frames)} frames, descriptor length {X.shape[1]}; {a.n} selected; "
          f"max remaining distance {dmin.max():.4f} (first pick distance scale {np.linalg.norm(X - X[sel[0]], axis=1).max():.4f})")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

```
--- old ---
def sf_I2(v, coa=1.60, n=3, layers='ABABCACA'):
    """basal I2 stacking fault: n x n hexagonal in-plane, len(layers) basal layers; third vector = layers * c/2 z +
    (C - A) in-plane, so the stacking continues periodically with one fault per period."""
    a = (2 * v / (np.sqrt(3) / 2 * coa)) ** (1 / 3); c = coa * a
    a1 = np.array([a, 0, 0]); a2 = np.array([-a / 2, a * np.sqrt(3) / 2, 0])
    site = {'A': np.array([0, 0]), 'B': np.array([1 / 3, 2 / 3]), 'C': np.array([2 / 3, 1 / 3])}
    t = site['C'] - site['A']
    cell = np.array([n * a1, n * a2, len(layers) * c / 2 * np.array([0, 0, 1]) + t[0] * a1 + t[1] * a2])
    pos = []
    for k, L in enumerate(layers):
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                s = site[L] + [i, j]
                pos.append(s[0] * a1 + s[1] * a2 + np.array([0, 0, k * c / 2]))
    return cell, np.array(pos)
```

### Claude (11-21 15:26)

I've written and tested the three loop tools. The test turned up a problem: every twin-boundary DFT frame failed, so I submitted a small fix test.

**The tools** (in `~/Claude/tools`):
- **`fe_dp_explore.py`** sets up the MD runs and their GPU job, plus each round's training job. It covers 11 cells at 0–350 GPa and 300 K up to 1.05 T_m, 275 runs of 20 ps each.
  - Cells: perfect hcp and fcc; hcp with 1 or 2 vacancies; a basal I₂ stacking fault (72 atoms); the Σ7 tilt boundary and the twin; and sheared copies of hcp, vacancy, Σ7 and twin.
  - The sheared runs oscillate a 2 % xz shear with a 2 ps period, the same kind of strain as the anelastic runs.
- **`fe_dp_sample.py`** picks frames from each run with SOAP + FPS (3 per run by default). It drops collapsed frames and sets up the DFT directories and task list for the existing VASP job script.
- **`fe_dp_split.py`** runs the previous model against DFT on those frames. The worst 15 % in each temperature band go to training, the rest to the test set. It then writes the next `input.json` for a 200k-step restart from the previous model.
  - Frames already inside the error targets are not added, so a round that adds almost nothing means the potential has converged.
  - `split_summary.txt` gives error percentiles and a converged yes/no for each band.

**Testing:** our own model doesn't exist yet, so I used Xin's PBEsol model as a stand-in.
- **MD:** 8 short runs on a P100 ran at about 500 steps/s, so a 20 ps run takes about 40 s and all 275 runs about 3–4 GPU-hours. Pressure held at 300 GPa, and the shear runs oscillated as intended.
- **Sampling:** 24 DFT directories were set up correctly.
- **Splitting:** it ran on the 585 finished R1 frames and put 88 in training and 497 in test. Xin's model's errors are large only because it uses a different functional, which is expected.

The step-by-step commands for one round are in `ML/DP/README.md`, and §3.2 of the plan now lists the tools.

**Problems found:**
1. **The twin frames are unusable as set up.** All 50 twin frames from the defect batch failed. The SCF diverged to about −10¹⁰ eV and each frame hit the 200-step / 8-hour limit; that is charge sloshing in the 75 Å twin cell. The Σ7 frames (22 Å cell) converged, but slowly, in about 100 steps; vacancies all finished.
   - I submitted job 7578197, three DFT settings on one twin frame: two with damped charge mixing and one with direct minimisation.
   - Whichever converges goes into a rerun of the 50 frames and into `fe_dp_sample.py`, because the loop's twin runs would hit the same problem.
2. **I relaxed the band-occupation check from 1e-3 to 1e-2.** This follows your rule to relax tolerances that don't converge.
   - The stricter check threw out 38 frames, all at 0 GPa and 1300–1700 K, including 24 of the 25 fcc frames at 1700 K. Their highest band held only 0.0013–0.0053 electrons, which makes no meaningful difference to energies or forces.
   - The change applies to the first training job (7336710), which hasn't started yet. It will now keep those frames and train without the twin frames.

**Progress:** everything else is done, including all the earlier recalculations and 160 of the 210 defect frames. The last defect task is a twin frame that will time out in about 30 minutes, and then training job 7336710 starts. Once it produces its compressed model, round 01 begins with `fe_dp_explore.py DP 01 --model DP/00/graph_c.pb`.

```
# Plan: vacancy free energies, diffusion and dislocations in MgO and MgSiO₃ (2026-10-13)

**RC request (10-13):**
1. Do the free-energy integrations of Ita & Cohen (1997, 1998) to get vacancy formation free energies and diffusion rates.
2. Put in dislocations: Guan et al. (2026) report a slip-system change in bridgmanite at about 1800 K.
3. Compare with Perez et al. (2025) for MgO at high strain rate.

Papers are in `Papers/`:
- Ita & Cohen, PRL 79, 3198 (1997): `PhysRevLett.79.3198.pdf`.
- Ita & Cohen, GRL 25, 1095 (1998): `Ita_et_al-1998-...pdf`.
- Cordier et al., Nature 613, 303 (2023): `s41586-022-05410-9.pdf`.
- Guan et al., Commun. Earth Environ. 7, 183 (2026): `s43247-026-03212-9.pdf` and its SI.
- Perez et al., PRB 111, 144108 (2025): `Perez.pdf`.

## 0. Why this matters, and what the papers set up

- **Cordier et al. 2023.**
  - Claim: periclase deforms 10³–10⁷× more slowly than bridgmanite at mantle strain rates, so the lower mantle's rheology is that of bridgmanite.
  - Basis: climb in MgO is limited by O self-diffusion, which they take from the **Ita & Cohen fit** (their Eq. 1, Table 1). D_O falls to 10⁻³¹ m²/s at 90–120 GPa.
  - Bridgmanite side: pure climb creep (Reali et al. 2019) with an assumed vacancy fraction $X_v=10^{-5}$.
  - The conclusion therefore rests on (i) D_O(P,T) in MgO and (ii) diffusion in bridgmanite. Both are what an Ita–Cohen-type calculation gives, and DeePMD can now do it for both minerals with the same model.
  - *Note:* Cordier Table 1 lists $E_0=0.4\times10^{-19}$ J. Their Table 2 enthalpies (9.15 eV at 30 GPa, 15.09 eV at 120 GPa) are reproduced only with Ita & Cohen's $E_0\approx9.4\times10^{-19}$ J (5.9 eV) for O. The 0.4 appears to be a typo; only Table 1 is affected.
- **Guan et al. 2026** (25 GPa, 1700–2100 K, strain rates 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁴ s⁻¹):
  - The dominant slip system changes at about 1800 K, from [010](100) below to [100](010) above.
  - The authors argue that dislocation creep, not diffusion or pure climb creep, may control the lower mantle.
  - The mechanism of the change is unknown. A temperature-dependent crossover of the lattice friction (Peierls stress) or mobility of the two systems is the obvious candidate, and MD can test it directly.
- **Perez et al. 2025** (laser-driven Richtmyer–Meshkov):
  - Solid single-crystal MgO has an effective viscosity of at most about $10^2$ Pa s at 175 ± 15 GPa, about 3500 K and $\dot\varepsilon=10^6$–$10^7$ s⁻¹. That implies a flow stress of about 1 GPa or less.
```

```
## 5k. Edge-dislocation drag in MgO at 175 GPa / 3500 K and the Perez et al. (2025) bound (2026-10-13)

Full write-up: `results_dislocations/MGO_EDGE_DISLOCATION_RESULTS.md`. Run: job 4452807.
- **Setup:** ½[110](001) edge dislocation, 8232 atoms, MgO-only DeePMD model; τ = 0.1–1 GPa applied through rigid blocks.
- **Superseded 2026-11-15 (§5m):** B = 1.76 × 10⁻⁴ Pa s with no threshold down to 0.15 GPa; the values below used a top block that was not rigid.
- **Drag:** viscous glide at τ ≥ 0.5 GPa with $v=b\tau/B$ and **B = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ Pa s**. No steady glide at τ ≤ 0.25 GPa: either a threshold or too short a run (100 ps runs to follow).
- **Effective viscosity:** $\eta_{eff}=B/(\rho b^2)$ = 330, 33, 3.3 and 0.33 Pa s for ρ = 10¹³, 10¹⁴, 10¹⁵ and 10¹⁶ m⁻².
  - This meets Perez's η ≤ 10² Pa s for ρ ≳ 3 × 10¹³ m⁻², or about 10¹⁴ m⁻² with orientation factors.
  - Drag-limited flow stress at 10⁷ s⁻¹ is ≤ 0.33 GPa for ρ ≥ 10¹⁴ m⁻², so the ≲ 1 GPa strength is set by the threshold, not drag.
- **Granato–Lücke:** with this B, string damping (plan Eq. 13) peaks at 7 kHz for L = 100 µm and needs L ≈ 1 cm for 1 Hz. Drag-controlled dislocation loss is not a seismic-band mechanism; kink-pair or pinning processes would be needed.

## 5l. MgO models against DFT and experiment (2026-10-14)

Full write-up: `results_dft/MGO_DFT_MODEL_COMPARISON.md`; figure `results_dft/mgo_dft_model_comparison.pdf/png`.

VASP PBEsol single points (Deng training settings) were run on 8 MD frames each of perfect and bound-pair MgO (512/510 atoms) at 20 GPa / 2000 K and 140 GPa / 3000 K. Each frame was scored with both DeePMD models; the experimental EOS is Tange et al. 2009.

  - Deng ≈ PBEsol (ΔP ≤ 0.3 GPa at fixed V); within 2.3 GPa of experiment.
```

**Tool `Bash`** — Check coordination and gaps in tw13 cells

```
R1=/groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/VASP/Fe/hcp_fcc/ML/R1; ~/cohen_env/bin/python - <<EOF
from ase.io import read
from ase.neighborlist import neighbor_list
import numpy as np
for d in ['def/tw13_P0_T300/recal/1','def/tw13_P300_T300/recal/1','def/s7_P0_T300/recal/1']:
    a=read('$R1/'+d+'/POSCAR'); dn=(np.sqrt(2)*a.get_volume()/len(a))**(1/3)

    n=a.cell.array[2]; n=np.cross(a.cell.array[0],a.cell.array[1]); n/=np.linalg.norm(n)
    z=(a.positions@n); z=np.sort(z%abs(a.cell.array[2]@n))
    print(d, 'CN hist', np.bincount(cn), 'max gap along normal %.2f A'%np.max(np.diff(np.r_[z, z[0]+abs(a.cell.array[2]@n)])))
EOF
```

### Claude (11-21 15:33)

You're right on the first point, and I've stopped using Xin's model. On the SCF divergence I think the evidence still points to charge sloshing, so I'm arguing that one below.

**Xin's model.** I used it only to check that the new scripts ran, because our model doesn't exist yet. Nothing from it went into our data, and that test directory is now deleted. I've saved a rule never to use it, even for tests. The loop runs as you describe:
- Training job 7336710 fits model 00 on our own DFT frames: about 640 so far, R1, R1b and the finished defect frames. It starts when the last defect task ends, in under half an hour.
- MD with model 00 on our cells, then sample frames, DFT, add the worst 10–20 %, retrain, and repeat.

**Twin SCF divergence.** I looked for a setup error and didn't find one:
- **Geometry:** VASP's own neighbour table shows nearest neighbours at 2.28–2.53 Å at 0 GPa. There are no overlapping or duplicate atoms, and the volume (10.5 Å³/atom) matches the other cells.
- **Inputs:** PAW_PBE Fe_sv, 1600 electrons and 848 bands (800 needed) are all correct, and the k-mesh is 7×3×1.
- **VASP's own warning:** at startup it says "One of the lattice vectors is very long (>50 Å), but AMIN is rather large… charge sloshing might occur along the long lattice vector… try to decrease AMIN to 0.01."
- **Trend with cell length:** median SCF steps are 41 for the vacancy cells (about 8–10 Å) and 63 for Σ7 (22 Å), which also overshoots early and then recovers. The 75 Å twin never recovers, and its charge-density error grows to about 10³ before the energy runs off.

I did not use VASP's suggested fix in my first test, so I've added an AMIN = 0.01 run (job 7580023). It joins the three charge-mixing variants already queued (7578197), all on the same frame. If AMIN or the mixing changes converge, it was sloshing. If all four still diverge, you're right that something else is wrong, and I'll rebuild the twin cell and test that directly.

One real flaw in the twin cell itself: one boundary atom has only 5 neighbours and three have 7. That comes from removing the 4 boundary atoms that sat too close (rm_ratio). It shouldn't break the SCF, but the boundary is poorly built and worth rebuilding either way.

**Dislocations in the MgO / MgSiO₃ work.**
- **The anelastic runs have none.** The oscillatory shear sweeps used perfect crystals, vacancy cells, Σ5 bicrystals and the MgO polycrystal.
- **There was one separate dislocation study:** a driven MgO ½[110](001) edge dislocation at about 162 GPa and 3500 K. It gave phonon drag B = 1.76 × 10⁻⁴ Pa s with no threshold. Its Granato–Lücke damping peaks at about 7 kHz for 100 µm lines, so free glide is not a seismic-band loss.
- **Not done:** the bridgmanite dislocations (Guan's two slip systems) were planned but never run. Drag versus temperature (QUESTIONS item 9) is still waiting for your decision.

**Do the vacancy runs make dislocations by themselves?** No, and we shouldn't expect them to:
- **Loops from vacancies:** a dislocation loop forms when tens of vacancies gather into a disc that collapses. That needs a supersaturation and diffusion over far longer than nanoseconds. Our vacancy number is fixed, and in MgO most vacancies sit in bound pairs.
- **Nucleation by stress:** creating dislocations in a perfect lattice needs stresses near the ideal strength, about G/10 or tens of GPa at these pressures. Our sweeps reach a few GPa at 1–3 % strain.
- **Cell size:** cells a few nm across can't hold a loop big enough to be stable.
- **What has moved:** the boundary sliding and migration we saw in Σ5 move steps that carry dislocation character, but those stay inside the boundary.
- **Not checked:** nobody has scanned the polycrystal or the 3 % strain bicrystal trajectories for lattice dislocations.

**So yes, we need them.** Seismic-band loss from dislocations would come from pinned line segments, kink-pair (Peierls) motion, or dislocation–boundary interaction. Each of these needs dislocations put into the cell and driven, as in the edge-dislocation runs.

For Fe that has two consequences:
- The training set must contain dislocation cores before the production dislocation runs.
- I recommend adding small periodic cells holding pairs of ⟨a⟩ screw and edge dislocations, about 100–200 atoms, on the basal and prismatic planes, to the exploration systems from round 01. That way the cores are trained alongside the vacancies and boundaries.

Should I add those Fe dislocation cells to round 01, and scan the existing MgO trajectories for dislocations?

I've set up your recipe on the same twin frame (job 7584758). I cancelled my four charge-mixing tests before any of them started.

The grid supports your point. VASP's default grid for the twin cell is coarser along the long cell axis, which is the short reciprocal axis:

| axis | grid points | equivalent cutoff (a.u.) |
|---|---|---|
| short a (2.5 Å) | 24 | 16.2 |
| b (5.7 Å) | 50 | 14.6 |
| long c (75 Å) | 648 | 14.4 |

VASP's startup output also recommends `LREAL = Auto` for a cell this large.

The three test runs (directories in `R1/scftest/`):

| run | settings | purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `tw13_lreal_grid_amin` | `LREAL = Auto`, `AMIN = 0.01`, NGY 50→56, NGZ 648→768, fine grid at twice these | your full recipe; all three axes now at 16.2 a.u. |
| `tw13_lreal` | `LREAL = Auto` only | shows whether LREAL alone is enough |
| `s7_lreal_grid_amin` | Σ7 frame at 0 GPa, 300 K with `LREAL = Auto` and `AMIN = 0.01` | consistency check, below |

**Consistency check:** every other training frame uses `LREAL = .FALSE.`. That Σ7 frame already converged with `.FALSE.`, so rerunning it with the new settings gives the energy and force difference that `LREAL = Auto` would add to the training data. If the difference is a few meV/atom or more, I'd keep the twin frames consistent another way. Each twin frame would first converge with `LREAL = Auto`, then restart once with `.FALSE.` from that density. That needs `LWAVE` and `LCHARG` turned on.

If the full recipe converges, I'll rerun the 50 twin frames with it. The same settings will also go into `fe_dp_sample.py` for twin cells, because the loop's twin runs would otherwise fail the same way.

The training job (7336710) still waits for the last defect task, a twin frame due to hit its 8-hour limit within minutes. It will train without the twin frames.

```
# Plan: dislocation and grain-boundary rheology from driven MD and stress-dependent rates, down to seismic frequencies

*2026-10-15. RC: "I think that driving the system with strains would help overcome the need to find the collective motions by random chance. I would concentrate on dislocations and grain boundaries. If we know the grain boundary rheology we can model effects of grain size."*

## 0. Idea

NEMD and Green–Kubo stop near 1 GHz. Equilibrium kinetic Monte Carlo reaches lower frequencies, but only for events it can find. The events that matter here (kink pairs, unpinning, disconnection nucleation, coupled boundary migration) are collective and rare, so random search will not find them. Instead:

1. **Drive** (stress, strain rate, large-amplitude oscillation) so the collective events happen within MD time. MD then *finds* the mechanism and gives its rate at high stress.
2. **Anchor at low stress** with NEB/string calculations along the discovered path at τ = 0 and intermediate τ. Add biased sampling (PLUMED, with the driven coordinate as the collective variable) where entropy matters.
3. **Fit a transition-state rate law** for each mechanism. Kocks–Argon–Ashby form:

$$r(\tau,T)=\nu\exp\!\left[-\frac{\Delta G(\tau)}{k_BT}\right],\qquad \Delta G(\tau)=\Delta G_0\left[1-\left(\frac{\tau}{\tau_c}\right)^{p}\right]^{q},\qquad \Omega^\ast=-\frac{\partial\Delta G}{\partial\tau} \tag{1}$$

   With forward and backward events, the net velocity of a defect with step length λ is

$$v=\lambda\,\nu\,e^{-\Delta G_0/k_BT}\,2\sinh\!\left(\frac{\tau\,\Omega^\ast_0}{k_BT}\right)\quad(\tau\ll\tau_c) \tag{2}$$

   This gives the **linear-response** (seismic-amplitude, τ ≲ 1 MPa) mobility
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Build a B1 MgO slab containing one 1/2[110](001) edge dislocation (high-pressure slip system), for mobility runs.

Orientation: x = [110] (Burgers vector and glide direction, repeat b = a/sqrt2), y = [001] (glide-plane normal,
repeat a), z = [1-10] (dislocation line, repeat a/sqrt2). Periodic in x and z; finite in y (rigid blocks at both ends).
Two-block construction (Osetsky & Bacon 2003): the lower half has NX+1 repeats along x and the upper half NX repeats,
both strained to Lx = (NX + 1/2) b, so one edge dislocation (b along x) sits on the (001) plane between the halves.
Atoms in the bottom and top NRIGID repeats along y are written as separate types so LAMMPS can group them:
    type 1 Mg, 2 O (mobile); 3 Mg, 4 O (bottom rigid); 5 Mg, 6 O (top rigid)   [MgO-only model: use pair_coeff with
    the type map 'Mg O Mg O Mg O' -> tools/disl_drive.lammps maps them].
usage: build_mgo_edge_slab.py --a 3.70 --nx 24 --ny 14 --nz 6 --nrigid 1 --out FILE [--perfect]
--perfect builds the same slab with NX repeats in both halves (reference cell, no dislocation).
"""
import argparse
import numpy as np

def unit_cell(a):
    """Atoms of rocksalt in the orthogonal cell (a/sqrt2, a, a/sqrt2) with x=[110], y=[001], z=[1-10]."""
    R = np.array([[1, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1], [1, -1, 0]], float); R /= np.linalg.norm(R, axis=1)[:, None]
    L = np.array([a / np.sqrt(2), a, a / np.sqrt(2)])
    fcc = np.array([[0, 0, 0], [.5, .5, 0], [.5, 0, .5], [0, .5, .5]])
    pts, typ = [], []
    for i in range(-3, 4):
        for j in range(-3, 4):
            for k in range(-3, 4):
                for f in fcc:
                    for t, sh in ((1, [0, 0, 0]), (2, [.5, 0, 0])):
                        r = R @ ((f + sh + [i, j, k]) * a)
                        s = r / L
                        if np.all(s > -1e-6) and np.all(s < 1 - 1e-6):
                            pts.append(s); typ.append(t)
    pts, typ = np.array(pts), np.array(typ)
    assert len(pts) == 4 and (typ == 1).sum() == 2, (len(pts), typ)
    return pts, typ, L

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--a', type=float, required=True); ap.add_argument('--nx', type=int, default=24)
    ap.add_argument('--ny', type=int, default=14); ap.add_argument('--nz', type=int, default=6)
    ap.add_argument('--nrigid', type=int, default=1); ap.add_argument('--out', required=True)
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Set up a frequency sweep of oscillatory-shear NEMD runs (anelastic_sweep.lammps).

Amplitude rule (shear strain):  gamma0 = clip(gdot0 / w, gmin, gmax)              (Eq. 1)
  constant strain-rate amplitude gdot0 keeps the Weissenberg number gdot0*tau fixed,
  gmin keeps the stress signal above noise at high frequency, gmax caps large strains.

Run length from the fluctuation-dissipation estimate of the lock-in error on G'':
  dsigma^2 = C kT G''(w) / (w V T_run)                                            (Eq. 2)
  rel. error  e = dsigma / (G'' gamma0)  ->  T_run = C kT / (w G'' V gamma0^2 e^2)  (Eq. 3)
C = 8 was calibrated on the 8000 K, 1 THz, gamma0 = 0.0066 shear run (54671682).
G''(w) is guessed from a Maxwell model  G* = Ginf i w tau / (1 + i w tau)         (Eq. 4)
T_run is then raised to at least ncyc_min periods and rounded up to whole chunks.

Uniaxial mode (--mode uniaxial, fix deform x wiggle, M* = K* + 4/3 G*):
  fixed strain amplitude eps0; lx amplitude = eps0 * Lx                           (Eq. 5)
  M''(w) from a Maxwell guess  M* = M0 + dM i w tau / (1 + i w tau)                (Eq. 6)
  dM = 281 GPa with tau = 0.057 ps reproduces M'' = 89 GPa at 1 THz (R1A1, eps0 = 0.033);
  Eq. 3 with M'' and eps0 in place of G'' and gamma0; C = 0.74 from the R1A1 error bar,
  default C = 1 in this mode.
T_run is capped at tmax_ps (if given); the expected error is then printed.
```

### Claude (11-21 16:05)

I've set up dislocation cells for MgO, bridgmanite and Fe, started one MgO pilot run, and written the plan. I also found and fixed a mistake that had left the defect frames out of model 00's training. The single twin SCF test is running in the debug queue.

**1. Twin SCF test (job 7585759, debug queue, 30 min).** I'm running only your full recipe, on the frame that failed: `LREAL = Auto`, `AMIN = 0.01`, and a finer FFT grid along the short reciprocal axis (NGY 50→56, NGZ 648→768, so all three axes have the same cutoff). The other variants were cancelled before they started.
- It has done 7 SCF steps. The energy is −962 eV at step 7. The failed run was at −8,496 eV there, and at −26,000 eV by step 11.
- It isn't converged yet, and 30 minutes gives only about 15 steps. If it stays well-behaved, I'll rerun one twin frame to full convergence before touching the other 49.

**2. Model 00 was training without the defect frames.** Slurm runs the copy of a job script saved at submission. I had added the vacancy and Σ7 frames to the script after submitting job 7336710, so it was training on 468 frames with none of them.
- I cancelled it about 10 minutes in, at 20k of 600k steps, and resubmitted it as job 7588075.
- It now includes 155 defect frames: 100 vacancy and 55 Σ7. It also keeps the 38 low-pressure frames recovered by the relaxed band check.
- 20k steps took about 10 minutes, so the full training should take about 5 hours.

**3. Dislocations.**
- **Cell builder** (`~/Claude/tools/build_dislocation_dipole.py`): it makes fully periodic cells containing a pair of opposite-sign dislocations, edge or screw, for MgO, bridgmanite or hcp Fe. The glide plane is set up so the existing xz shear sweeps drive the dislocations directly.
  - Edge cells remove one whole column of repeat units, so they stay stoichiometric and keep the perfect cell's volume per atom.
  - Built and checked: the MgO ½[110](001) edge (3968 atoms) and screw (4096), the {110} edge, bridgmanite [100](010) and [010](100) edges and the [100] screw (1920–2400 atoms), and four Fe cells.
  - The closest pair of atoms is 1.28–1.95 Å, which minimisation should fix.
- **MgO pilot (job 7587907, P100 debug queue, waiting for the debug slot):**
  - The edge cell is at the volume of the MgO production runs (≈162–180 GPa), 4000 K, with the MgO-only model.
  - The run minimises and then runs 40 ps at constant temperature. `disl_dipole_cores.py` then checks that both cores formed and stay on their glide planes.
  - Only after that do I run a shear sweep against the existing perfect-crystal reference.
- **Fe training:** four dislocation cells (88–176 atoms) plus two sheared versions are now in the round-01 MD systems, so their frames go through the same DFT loop. The four are an edge gliding on the basal plane, an edge gliding on the prism plane, and screws gliding on each.
- **Plan** (`ANELASTICITY_PLAN_DISLOCATION_Q.md`):
  - The sweeps measure the dislocations' relaxation directly (Eq. 3). I expect a peak near 1 THz in the pilot cell, and two cell sizes separate the drag coefficient B from the cell's own back-stress.
  - That B goes into a pinned-line (Granato–Lücke) model for kHz to seismic frequencies (Eqs. 4–5). The lattice-friction rates from the planned driven runs come in where friction controls glide, which is certainly the case in bridgmanite.
  - Dislocation creep (Eq. 6), using our own diffusion results, covers years to Gy.
  - Eq. 7 combines all the loss mechanisms over 10¹² to 10⁻¹⁷ Hz.
  - Rough MgO check: with our measured B, the free-glide peak is near 10⁸ Hz at a density of 10¹² m⁻², and reaches seismic frequencies only for line segments of about 1 cm. That could be the "unimportant" answer for MgO.

**Decisions for you:**
1. **Slip systems:** MgO ½⟨110⟩{100} only, or {110} as well? Bridgmanite Guan's two systems, plus [001](010)?
2. **Scope:** the full set at about 300 P100-hours (2 sizes × 3 temperatures for each system), or a reduced first pass at about 60 P100-hours?

### Claude (11-21 16:11)

You're right on the principle, but that is how the grid is already set up: it isn't backwards, and only the long axis is slightly overshot. The k-point mesh is unchanged.

**FFT grid.** The point count along an axis grows with the real cell length on that axis. The same count fixes how many G-vectors fit along the matching reciprocal vector, so "more points along the long real axis" and "fewer along the short reciprocal axis" are one requirement. VASP's default already gave the long 75 Å axis the most points (648, against 24 along the 2.46 Å axis). What I changed is the number of points per Å, i.e. the effective cutoff on each axis:

| axis | length | default | points/Å | my test | points/Å |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | 2.46 Å | 24 | 9.8 | 24 | 9.8 |
| b | 5.71 Å | 50 | 8.8 | 56 | 9.8 |
| c (long) | 74.8 Å | 648 | 8.7 | 768 | 10.3 |

The default was about 11 % coarser along c than along a. My 768 overshoots the other axes slightly. NGZ = 720 (9.6 points/Å) sits in the middle and is a valid FFT size, so I'll use 720 from now on.

**k-points.** The mesh is still 7×3×1 (11 k-points). The long axis already has only 1 k-point. The 7 is along the 2.46 Å axis, and comes from requiring n × L ≥ 16 Å, the same density as the 2×2×2 mesh on the 64-atom bulk cells. If you think 16 Å is more than needed, 6×3×1 (14.8 Å) would cut the cost, but it would be less dense than the bulk cells.

**Test status (job 7585759, debug queue).** At step 11 the energy is −832 eV, about −8.3 eV per atom, and the density residual has dropped to 190 from 592 at step 8. The old run of this frame was at −26,000 eV by step 11. It won't converge within 30 minutes; the job ends in about 10 minutes.

**Next.** If it stays healthy to the end, I'll run this one frame to full convergence in the regular queue: `LREAL = Auto`, `AMIN = 0.01`, NGY 56, NGZ 720. Only if that converges will I rerun the other 49 twin frames.

### Claude (11-21 16:17)

The single 1 along the twin's long axis is already Γ along that axis, so it's fine as it stands. A Monkhorst–Pack mesh with n = 1 puts that k-component at 0. The sampling length along that axis is 1 × 74.8 Å, more than four times the 16 Å target and the 17 Å of the 2×2×2 mesh on the 64-atom bulk cells. A 1 only hurts a metal along a short axis, and the mesh rule never gives one there.

If you want even meshes on every axis, 6×2×2 is the option, but it doubles the k-points and the cost per SCF step. I'd keep 6×2×1.

**Even-mesh rule.** `kpoints_auto` (in `fe_r1d_defects.py`, also used by the iteration-loop sampling tool) now lowers any odd count above 1 by one. The twin becomes 6×2×1 (was 7×3×1) and Σ7 becomes 4×2×1 (was 5×3×1). The 55 Σ7 frames that already finished used 5×3×1, which is close in sampling density, so I'm keeping them.

**Twin tests:**
- The debug test (job 7585759) is now converging steadily. At step 15 the energy is −820 eV (about −8.2 eV per atom), the change per step is down to +27 eV, and the density residual has fallen from 140 at step 13 to 68. The old settings had reached −10¹⁰ eV.
- The full single-frame run is submitted as job 7590878, in the regular queue with an 8-hour limit. It uses `LREAL = Auto`, `AMIN = 0.01`, NGZ 720, NGY 56 and the 6×2×1 mesh. If it converges, I'll rerun the other 49 twin frames with the same settings.

     - Floor: frames already inside the A2 targets are not added (3 meV/atom; 0.15 eV/Å up to 0.7 Tm; 10 % of RMS|F| above).
     - Upper cutoffs 10 drop broken frames.
     - Retrain with `--init-frz-model`, 200k steps.
     - Convergence: the top-fraction cutoffs fall below the A2 targets.

   - **Periodic dislocation dipoles** (driven by xz shear):
     - Edge: remove one column of whole units between z = Lz/4 and 3Lz/4; apply the isotropic Volterra edge field with images and the spurious linear terms removed; Lx shrinks by b/2.
     - Screw: quadrupolar arrangement, tilt xz = xy = b/2, β_ij = b_i A_j/V.
   - **Analysis model:**
     - Bẋ = bσ − kx.
     - Debye relaxation: ΔJ = ρb²/k, τ = B/(k + ρb²G).
     - Granato–Lücke: τ_L = BL²/(π²C), f_peak = πCρ/(2B).
     - Kink-pair mobility at low stress.

**Tool `Bash`** — Summarize dp test errors by group

```
cd /groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/VASP/Fe/hcp_fcc/ML/DP/00; python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
s=open('dptest.log').read()
blk=re.findall(r'testing system : (\S+).*?number of test data : (\d+).*?Energy RMSE/Natoms : (\S+) eV.*?Force  RMSE        : (\S+)',s,re.S)
from collections import defaultdict
g=defaultdict(lambda:[0,0,0])
rows=[]
for n,k,e,f in blk:
    k=int(k);e=float(e);f=float(f); grp=n.split('/')[-1].split('_')[0]+('_'+n.split('_')[1] if n.split('/')[-1].startswith('def') else '')
    g[grp][0]+=k; g[grp][1]+=k*e*e; g[grp][2]+=k*f*f; rows.append((e,f,k,n))
for k,v in sorted(g.items()): print(f"{k:14} n={v[0]:4d} E {1e3*(v[1]/v[0])**.5:7.2f} meV/at  F {(v[2]/v[0])**.5:.3f}")
print('worst E'); [print(f"  {r[3]:32} n{r[2]} E {1e3*r[0]:.1f} F {r[1]:.3f}") for r in sorted(rows)[-12:]]
EOF
grep -n "numb_steps\|start_lr\|stop_lr\|limit_pref\|start_pref" input.json; awk 'NR>1 && $1%50000==0' lcurve.out
```

**Tool `Bash`** — Per-system energy offsets for all training data

```
cd /groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/VASP/Fe/hcp_fcc/ML/DP/00; source ~/.bashrc >/dev/null 2>&1; conda activate /central/groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/anaconda2/deepmd_py311; export TMPDIR=/resnick/groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/tmp CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=; S=/resnick/groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/tmp/claude-25175/-resnick-home-recohen-Claude-Anelasticity/b662d795-e17c-4f1f-98bf-5406b2fd0e6d/scratchpad; python - > $S/offsets.txt 2>/dev/null <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, glob, os
from deepmd.infer import DeepPot
dp=DeepPot('graph_c.pb')
for d in sorted(glob.glob('data/*')):
    s=d+'/set.000'; c=np.load(s+'/coord.npy'); b=np.load(s+'/box.npy'); e=np.load(s+'/energy.npy'); fp=np.load(s+'/fparam.npy')
    t=np.loadtxt(d+'/type.raw',dtype=int).reshape(-1); n=len(t)
    E,F,V=dp.eval(c,b,t,fparam=fp.reshape(len(c),-1))
    de=(E.ravel()-e)/n; vol=np.abs(np.linalg.det(b.reshape(-1,3,3)))/n
    print(f"{os.path.basename(d):30} {len(c):3d} {n:4d} sig {fp.ravel()[0]:.4f} V {vol.mean():6.3f} E/at {e.mean()/n:8.4f} dE {1e3*de.mean():7.1f} sd {1e3*de.std():5.1f}")
EOF
sort -k12 -n $S/offsets.txt | awk '{print}' | head -15; echo ...; sort -k12 -n $S/offsets.txt | tail -15
```

### Claude (11-21 19:08)

Of three jobs that finished, two worked as planned. The third, DeePMD model 00, trained but misses the energy target at low temperature, so I've started a diagnostic retrain.

**1. Twin (tw13) DFT: fixed.**
- The single full test (job 7590878, `R1/scftest/tw13_full`) converged in 74 SCF steps (the limit is 200), at F = −813.33 eV, in 73 min.
- The old settings ran away to −10¹⁰ eV, so LREAL=Auto, AMIN 0.01, the larger FFT grid along the long axis and the even k-mesh fixed it.
- The 50 reruns (job 7591334) passed the convergence check and are running. Tasks 1–3 are behaving: two are at SCF steps 50–55 with dE ≈ 10⁻² eV. Tasks 4–50 are queued.

**2. DeePMD model 00 (job 7588075): trained, but energies miss the target.**
- It trained in 1.6 h on 623 frames from 126 systems; the twin frames are not included. I tested it on its own training data.
- Forces are 0.15–0.34 eV/Å (target 0.15 up to 0.7 Tm).
- Energies are off by 8 meV/atom on the old set and 23 meV/atom on the A1 set (target 3).
- The energy error is a constant offset per state:
  - 30–65 meV/atom at SIGMA ≤ 0.06 eV (300–700 K);
  - the model has hcp too high and fcc too low, so it underestimates the hcp–fcc difference by about 70–100 meV/atom;
  - the spread within a state is about 1 meV, and the offset is about 0 at SIGMA ≥ 0.3 eV;
  - virials match the DFT values.
- I suspected k-point error first, but the A0c2 test shows the shifted 2×2×2 mesh is within 2 meV/atom of 4³ at 300 K. So this is a fitting problem, not a data problem.
- My best guess is that energies are underweighted: at the end of training the force term outweighs the energy term by about 50×. The lcurve energy error never fell below about 5–15 meV.
- **Diagnostic retrain 00e (job 7612548, P100, about 2 h, `DP/00e`):** same data and network, energy weight ×10 (limit_pref_e 2 → 20).
- I'm holding iteration-01 MD until 00e is checked. A model that is 100 meV/atom off on hcp vs fcc would give wrong energies for twins, stacking faults and grain boundaries.

**3. MgO edge-dipole pilot (job 7587907): cores are stable.**
- It ran 37.8 of the planned 40 ps at 4000 K before the time limit.
- Both ½[110](001) cores stayed intact and on their glide planes, at z = 14.9 and 45.3 Å (Lz/4 and 3Lz/4). Each core has 35–80 atoms.
- The pair glides freely as a unit, crossing the 41.3 Å cell in about 10 ps. Their separation along x varies between −11 and +7 Å, which is consistent with the low phonon drag found earlier.
- ⟨P⟩ = 145.9 GPa, against 144.7 GPa for the perfect reference cell at the same volume. The cell's back stress shows as ⟨σ_xz⟩ ≈ −1.0 GPa.
- This passes the pilot check. The next step in the plan is the M1 sweep at 4000 K (periods 0.2, 1, 5 and 20 ps; about 10 P100-h), started from `eq.data`.

INPROGRESS.md is updated.

**Next:**
- Compare 00e with 00. If the offsets go, iteration 01 starts from 00e, and the 50 twin frames go into its training set.
- Say if you want the M1 sweep submitted now. Your two decisions on the dislocation plan are still open: which slip systems, and the full set (about 300 P100-h) or the reduced pass (about 60).

### Claude (11-21 19:14)

I checked, and it isn't enthalpy versus energy. Every frame's label is the same quantity, VASP's free energy (TOTEN).

- **Same label everywhere.** `fe_dp_collect.py` reads TOTEN from OUTCAR with dpdata's `vasp/outcar` reader, for every set (old, old_b, A1, defects). For the first frame of three A1 states, the stored `energy.npy` value matches the OUTCAR TOTEN exactly:

  | state | TOTEN, 64 atoms (eV) |
  |---|---|
  | hcp P100, 300 K | −505.80594 |
  | fcc P200, 300 K | −429.32729 |
  | hcp P200, 300 K | −432.65109 |

- **Enthalpy would be far too big.** At 100 GPa, PV is about 0.62 eV/Å³ × 8.4 Å³ ≈ 5 eV per atom. That is roughly 100 times the 30–65 meV/atom offsets. It would also have the same sign for hcp and fcc at the same pressure. Instead hcp is +36 and fcc −31 meV/atom at 200 GPa.
- **The other VASP energies don't fit either.** At 300 K, TOTEN differs from "energy without entropy" by −2.0 meV/atom and from E(σ→0) by −1.0 meV/atom. That is too small, and the gap grows with temperature. The offsets do the opposite: they are largest at 300–700 K and near zero at high temperature.
- **No Pulay correction:** Pulay stress = 0 in the OUTCARs, and the model matches the DFT virials.

The retrain 00e (job 7612548, energy weight ×10) is still waiting in the GPU queue, and it should settle the question.
- If the offsets disappear and the forces stay at 0.15–0.34 eV/Å, a model consistent with all the labels exists, and model 00 simply underweighted energies.
- If they persist, there is a real inconsistency between states, and I would look next at the states' DFT inputs rather than the energy definition.

**Tool `Bash`** — Check energy-pressure consistency across states

```
cd /groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/VASP/Fe/hcp_fcc/ML/DP/00; /central/groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/anaconda2/deepmd_py311/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, glob
from scipy.optimize import least_squares
def bm_E(p,V):
    E0,V0,K,Kp=p; x=(V0/V)**(2/3)
    return E0+9*V0*K/16*((x-1)**3*Kp+(x-1)**2*(6-4*x))
def bm_P(p,V):
    E0,V0,K,Kp=p; x=(V0/V)**(2/3)
    return 1.5*K*(x**3.5-x**2.5)*(1+0.75*(Kp-4)*(x-1))
for ph in ['hcp','fcc']:
    E=[];V=[];P=[];lab=[]
    for d in sorted(glob.glob(f'data/a1_{ph}_P*_T300')):
        s=d+'/set.000'; n=64
        e=np.load(s+'/energy.npy').ravel()/n; b=np.load(s+'/box.npy').reshape(-1,3,3); v=np.load(s+'/virial.npy').reshape(-1,3,3)
        vol=np.abs(np.linalg.det(b))/n; p=np.trace(v,axis1=1,axis2=2)/3/vol/n
        E+=list(e);V+=list(vol);P+=list(p);lab+=[d.split('_')[2]]*len(e)
    E,V,P=map(np.array,(E,V,P))
    p0=[E.min(),V.max()*1.05,1.2,4.5]
    fe=least_squares(lambda p:bm_E(p,V)-E,p0).x
    fp=least_squares(lambda p:bm_P(p,V)-P,p0).x
    # E from the P-fit, with E0 adjusted to the mean
    Ep=bm_E(fp,V); Ep+= (E-Ep).mean()
    print(f'{ph}: E-fit V0 {fe[1]:.3f} K {fe[2]*160.2:.0f} GPa Kp {fe[3]:.2f} | P-fit V0 {fp[1]:.3f} K {fp[2]*160.
```

### Claude (11-21 19:29)

I've submitted the M1 sweep as job 7614205 (5 tasks, P100). It's pending.

**M1 setup** (in `.../Dislocations/M1_edge001_4000K`):
- It starts from the pilot's equilibrated cell `eq.data`: the ½[110](001) edge dipole, 3968 atoms, 4000 K, V6.6868. Each run first gets 5 ps of NVT with fresh velocities, the same as the perfect-crystal reference.
- **Drive:** xz shear on the (001) plane along [110]. For a cubic crystal this is the same c44 shear as the cube-aligned reference `4000K/FreqSweep_B1perfect`, so the two subtract directly.
- **Runs:**
  - periods 0.2, 1, 5 and 20 ps (5 THz to 50 GHz);
  - shear amplitude γ₀ = 0.01;
  - 200 ps each, with trajectories saved for tracking the cores.
- **Task 5** runs the perfect cell at the 20 ps period, because the existing reference only goes to 5 ps.
- At the pilot's speed of about 27 steps/s, each task takes about 2 h once it starts.
- **Analysis:** subtract the perfect-crystal modulus from the dipole cell's at each period, then fit plan Eq. 3. That gives the drag B, which I'll compare with the driven 1.76 × 10⁻⁴ Pa s, and the restoring stiffness k. I'll also track the cores against the drive phase.

**Fe energy problem: both retrains are now training.**
- 00e has the energy weight ×10 and 00f has it ×50; network and data are the same as model 00.
- The two together show whether the offsets fall as the energy weight rises.
- Model 00's baseline is in `DP/00/offsets.txt`:

  | electronic smearing σ (eV) | spread of the per-state energy offsets (rms, meV/atom) |
  |---|---|
  | < 0.07 | 27.6 |
  | > 0.4 | 3.7 |

  The scatter of frames within one state is only about 1–3 meV/atom.
- I wrote `tools/dp_state_offsets.py` to compute this per-state breakdown, and I'll run it on 00e and 00f when they finish.
- I also checked the DFT inputs behind every training set (A1, defects, old 128-atom), as far as the labels go:
  - all use the same POTCAR (Fe_sv), ENCUT 700, PREC Accurate, PBE, non-spin-polarized, 4 k-points;
  - the A1 "hcp" and "fcc" cells really are hcp and fcc, judging by their neighbor shells.

  So far nothing points to bad labels.

INPROGRESS.md is updated.

### Claude (11-21 19:40)

I've submitted the bridgmanite B1 pilot as job 7615044 (debug queue, 30 min). It's pending, waiting for a GPU.

**B1 pilot setup** (in `.../MgSiO3/1280atoms/V6.5669/crystal/Dislocations/B1_edge100_010_3000K`, with a README):
- **Cell:** the [100](010) edge dipole, 2400 atoms.
  - Burgers vector b = a = 4.445 Å; dislocation lines along [001].
  - Density ρ = 1.6 × 10¹⁷ m⁻².
  - Lattice taken from the equilibrated 3000 K crystal at V6.5669 (`crystal/Ladder/eq_3000.data` box divided by 4), so the volume per atom matches the production crystal.
- **Model:** Deng's bridgmanite model with fparam = kT, the same graph as the 3000 K crystal sweep `crystal/3000K/FreqSweep_solid`. Its type map is Mg, Si, O, which I checked.
- **Protocol:** the same as the MgO pilot — minimize, 40 ps of NVT, then check that both cores stay intact on their glide planes.
- **One thing to watch:** the closest atom pair in the built cell is 1.23 Å before minimization, a bit tighter than in MgO (1.28 Å). The minimizer should push it apart.
- If 30 min isn't enough to equilibrate bridgmanite cores, I'll extend the run in the regular queue.

**Other jobs**
- **M1 sweep (job 7614205):** the 0.2 ps task is running at 27.6 steps/s, so each of the five tasks needs about 2 h. Tasks 2–5 are queued.
- **00e and 00f retrains:** about 25 min into training, roughly 1.5 h to go. When they finish I'll compare their per-state energy offsets with model 00's.

INPROGRESS.md and the dislocation plan are updated.

```
cat /resnick/groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/tmp/claude-25175/-resnick-home-recohen-Claude-Anelasticity/b662d795-e17c-4f1f-98bf-5406b2fd0e6d/tasks/bou388lwu.output; cd /groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/VASP/Fe/hcp_fcc/ML/R1; source ~/cohen_env/bin/activate; python - <<'EOF'
import re
def rd(d):
    s=open(d+'/OUTCAR').read()
    E=float(re.findall(r'free  energy   TOTEN  =\s+(\S+)',s)[-1]); V=float(re.findall(r'volume of cell :\s+(\S+)',s)[-1])
    P=float(re.findall(r'external pressure =\s+(\S+) kB',s)[-1])/10; return E,V,P,'General timing' in s
for st in ['hcp_P100_T300','fcc_P100_T300','hcp_P200_T300','fcc_P200_T300']:
    Em,Vm,Pm,okm=rd(f'eostest/{st}_m'); Ep,Vp,Pp,okp=rd(f'eostest/{st}_p'); E0,V0,P0,_=rd(f'a1/{st}/recal/1')
    Pfd=-(Ep-Em)/(Vp-Vm)*160.2177
    # Simpson-like: average of the three stresses weighted for the central difference
    print(f'{st}: done {okm} {okp}  P_stress(V0) {P0:7.2f}  mean P(m,p) {0.5*(Pm+Pp):7.2f}  -dE/dV {Pfd:7.2f} GPa   diff {Pfd-(Pm+4*P0+Pp)/6:6.2f} GPa')
EOF
```

```
cd /groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/VASP/Fe/hcp_fcc/ML/R1; source ~/cohen_env/bin/activate; python - <<'EOF'
import os, shutil, numpy as np
from ase.io import read, write
from ase.io.vasp import read_vasp_out
tasks=[]

    src=f'a1/{st}/recal/1'; a=read(src+'/POSCAR'); o=read_vasp_out(src+'/OUTCAR'); F=o.get_forces()
    i=int(np.argmax(np.linalg.norm(F,axis=1))); u=F[i]/np.linalg.norm(F[i])
    for tag,s in (('m',-0.01),('p',0.01)):

        write(d+'/POSCAR',b,format='vasp',direct=True)
        for x in ('INCAR','KPOINTS','POTCAR'): shutil.copy(src+'/'+x,d+'/'+x)
        tasks.append(d)
    open(f'eostest/{st}_fdisp.txt','w').write(f'atom {i} (0-based) displaced +-0.01 A along unit {u.tolist()}; F.u = {F[i]@u:.5f} eV/A\n')

EOF
```

Summary:

2. **Key Technical Concepts**
   - **DeePMD se_e2_a descriptor:**
     - Generalized coordinates s(r)(1, r̂) give only ℓ = 0 and ℓ = 1 invariants: D_mn = scalar_m·scalar_n + vec_m·vec_n.
     - At centrosymmetric fcc sites and D3h hcp sites, the ℓ = 1 vector vanishes, so the descriptor is almost purely radial.
     - Measured: |D_fcc − D_hcp|/|D| = 0.4 %, against a 300 K thermal per-atom spread of 3–5 %.
   - **DFT (VASP) labels are verified self-consistent:**
     - All labels are TOTEN read by dpdata vasp/outcar.
     - Energy vs stress: −dE/dV − P ≈ 1.1 GPa, uniform across states.
     - Energy vs forces: finite difference agrees to 0.3 meV/Å.
     - k-mesh: the 64-atom cells with the 4-point shifted mesh are within 3–6 meV/atom of primitive cells at 24³.
     - True PBE non-magnetic ΔE(fcc−hcp) = 122.6 meV/atom at V = 7.25 Å³/atom (c/a 1.60).
   - **The model failure:**
     - Models predict ΔE(fcc−hcp) of 0–60 meV/atom.
     - The per-state offsets are hcp too high and fcc too low, largest at low SIGMA; within-state sd is only 1–4 meV.
     - Training on only the 300 K data, energy-only training, adding se_e3, and DPA-1 all fail.
     - The capacity limit is in the descriptor's resolution.
   - **Software environment:**
     - deepmd-kit 3.2.0 in deepmd_py311.
     - Its torch 2.12 is a CPU build (torch.version.cuda None).
     - The LAMMPS plugin has a PT backend library, but GPU PT models would need CUDA torch.
   - **Dislocation physics (plan Eqs. 1–7):**
     - Bẋ = bσ − kx.
     - Debye relaxation: ΔJ = ρb²/k, τ = B/(k + ρb²G).
     - Granato–Lücke string model.
   - **Bridgmanite core detection:** a CN classifier over all species is too broad (300+ "core" atoms). Use the Si sublattice instead (Si–Si first shell 3.0–3.4 Å, second shell 4.0–4.6 Å), with rc 3.6.

3. **Files and Code Sections**

   **New tool `~/Claude/tools/dp_state_offsets.py`.**
   - Per system it reports the mean and sd of dE = (E_model − E_DFT)/N (meV/atom), the force RMSE, sigma, V/atom and P.
   - It also gives group summaries (prefix before _P/_T) and summaries by SIGMA band (0–0.07, 0.07–0.2, 0.2–0.4, 0.4–1.0 eV).
   - Usage: `dp_state_offsets.py graph.pb data/ [--out offsets.txt]`, run with the deepmd_py311 python.
   - Key line: `E, F, Vir = dp.eval(c, b, t, fparam=fp)` with `e = np.load(...energy.npy).reshape(nf)`.
   - The reshape fixes an earlier broadcasting bug that produced a huge spurious sd.

   **Edited `~/Claude/tools/disl_dipole_cores.py`.**
   - Added `--sub T`, which keeps only atoms of type T so neighbours are counted within that sublattice:
   ```python
   ap.add_argument('--sub', type=int, help='use only the sublattice of this type')
   ...
   for step, H, ty, p in frames(a.dump):
       if a.sub is not None:
           m = ty == a.sub; ty, p = ty[m], p[m]
       buf.append((step, H, ty, p))
   ```

```
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Lock-in analysis of oscillatory-deformation MD (LAMMPS fix deform wiggle).

Fits stress and strain to  a + b t + sum_k [s_k sin(k w t) + c_k cos(k w t)]
at the KNOWN drive angular frequency w = 2 pi / period, k = 1..nharm.
Complex amplitudes at k=1 give the complex modulus
    M* = sigma_1 / eps_1 = M' + i M''      (Eq. 1)
    tan(delta) = M'' / M'                  (Eq. 2)
    eta'(w)    = M'' / w                   (Eq. 3)
Shear (xz): M* = G*.  Uniaxial (x): M* = K* + 4/3 G*  and M''/w = zeta + 4/3 eta.

Stress sign: sigma = -P_ab (LAMMPS pressure tensor), bar -> Pa (x1e5).
Error bars: the series is cut into nblock blocks of whole cycles and each block
is fit independently; std/sqrt(nblock) is reported.
Nonlinearity: |sigma_2|/|sigma_1| and |sigma_3|/|sigma_1| are printed.

Input: whitespace columns with a header line naming columns, e.g. the output of
extract_thermo.sh (Step ... Pxz ... Xz) or a fix ave/time file
(# TimeStep v_pxz v_xz v_lz).  Column names are matched case-insensitively
after stripping 'v_', 'c_', 'f_' prefixes.

Usage:
  anelastic_lockin.py FILE --period PS [--mode shear|uniaxial] [--dt 0.001] [--cols a,b,..]
                      [--L0 Å] [--skip-cycles 2] [--nblock 5] [--nharm 3]
"""
import argparse
import re
import sys
import numpy as np


def read_table(fname, cols=None):
    header = None
    rows = []
    with open(fname) as f:
        for line in f:
            s = line.strip()
            if not s:
                continue
            toks = s.lstrip('#').split()
```

### Claude (11-22 03:33)

I found and fixed the cause of the DeePMD energy offsets. It was the model's descriptor, not the DFT energies. A version with a three-body descriptor gets E(fcc) − E(hcp) = 124.4 meV/atom against DFT 122.6; the old model gives 54. The full retrain with that descriptor is now running as job 7715007. The M1 sweep also finished, but its response is nonlinear at γ₀ = 0.01, so a clean linear modulus can't be read from it.

## Fe DeePMD energy offsets

**The DFT labels are fine.** Every label is TOTEN, so there is no energy/enthalpy mix-up. Four direct checks agree:
- **Energy vs pressure:** −dE/dV − P = 1.1–1.2 GPa, the same for all four states tested.
- **Energy vs forces:** a finite-difference check matches the forces to 0.3 meV/Å.
- **k-mesh:** the 64-atom cells are within 3–6 meV/atom of primitive cells at 24³.
- **Perfect crystals:** E(fcc) − E(hcp) = 122.6 meV/atom at V = 7.25 Å³/atom.

**The cause is the se_e2_a descriptor.** It only carries angular information to ℓ = 1, and that term vanishes at fcc and hcp sites. The descriptor can then barely tell the two phases apart: they differ by 0.4 %, while thermal scatter within one state is 3–5 %.

**Tests**, all trained on only the ten 300 K hcp/fcc states:

| model | change | E(fcc) − E(hcp) (meV/atom; DFT 122.6) |
|---|---|---|
| 00 (all data) | none | 54 |
| 00e / 00f | energy weight ×10 / ×50 | 60 / 13 |
| 00t, 00tnv, 00tE, 00tEF | standard, no virial, energy only, energy ×500 | −5 to +1 |
| 00t3 | small three-body (se_e3) term | −0.6 |
| 00ta | DPA-1 | −1 |
| **00t3b** | **larger se_e3 term (rcut 4.5, sel 80, neuron [16,32,64])** | **124.4** |

With 00t3b, the per-state offsets drop to about 5.5 meV/atom rms (00t: 47 for fcc, 71 for hcp), and the forces also improve. It hit its 2 h limit at 93k of 100k steps, so its results come from the 93k checkpoint.

**Full retrain (`DP/00h`, job 7715007, running):**
- Model 00's input with the 00t3b descriptor.
- Energy weight 0.2 → 20, 600k steps.
- Data: all of model 00's data plus the twin data.
- At the end it runs dp test and the per-state offset check.

Training is about 9× slower than before, hence the 36 h limit. Resubmitting the script continues from the checkpoint. Iteration 01 will use 00h.

**Twin reruns:** all 50 converged (70–158 SCF steps, limit 200). They give 47 frames in 25 systems and are included in 00h.

## MgO M1 sweep (edge dipole, 4000 K)

| period | G′ (GPa) | G″ (GPa) | perfect crystal G′ / G″ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2 ps | 115 | 42 | 181 / −5 |
| 1 ps | 238 | −195 | 180 / −1 |
| 5 ps | −23 | 206 | 179 / 0 |
| 20 ps | −106 | 109 | 179 / −1 |

These are not a linear response: a negative G′ or G″ can't come from a linear, energy-absorbing system. The dipole flips between its two stable configurations every half cycle. The plastic strain swings ±0.015, which is 1.5 × γ₀, so the stress ends up opposite to the strain. At 4000 K the drive stress (1.8 GPa) is far above the switching stress in this cell.

Only the 0.2 ps run is near-linear. Read as free glide, it gives a drag coefficient B ≈ 9 × 10⁻⁵ Pa s, a factor of 2 from the driven value of 1.76 × 10⁻⁴. That is only an order-of-magnitude check, because the implied glide speed is about 0.8 of the shear-wave speed.

The Earth argument stands: with B ~ 10⁻⁴ Pa s, the drag-damped string peak lies at 1 MHz–10 GHz for loop lengths of 10–0.1 µm. Seismic attenuation from dislocations would have to come from thermally activated processes such as kink pairs or unpinning.

## Decision for you

To get a linear modulus from this cell, I propose one of two runs; neither is submitted:
1. **Long equilibrium run:** 1 ns NVT of the same cell (about 10 h on a P100), with G*(ω) from the stress autocorrelation. It is linear by construction and covers every frequency down to the inverse run length.
2. **Smaller drive:** γ₀ = 0.001 at 0.2 and 1 ps (2 × 2 h on a P100).

I'd do option 1. Which do you want?

### Claude (11-22 03:44)

I submitted the equilibrium (Green–Kubo) run as job 7718928. It is pending in the queue, so the trajectory setting can only be checked once it starts.

**What it runs**
- **Start:** the pilot's equilibrated dipole cell (3968 atoms, 4000 K, V6.6868), with the same MgO-only model as M1 and the perfect-crystal references.
- **Run:** 5 ps NVT, then 1 ns NVE, using the existing `gk_stress.lammps` and `gk_job.sh`. NVE is used so no thermostat affects the stress correlations.
- **Time:** about 10 h at the M1 speed (27.6 steps/s), within the 24 h limit. If it times out, resubmitting the same command continues from `restart.gk`.
- **Output:** stress every 2 steps, and the trajectory every 0.5 ps for tracking the cores.
- **Directory:** `/groups/carnegie_poc/rcohen/LAMMPS/MgO/4096atoms/V6.6868/4096atom/Dislocations/M1_edge001_4000K_GK`, with a README.

To write the trajectory I added an optional `DUMPN` variable to `~/Claude/tools/gk_stress.lammps`. It defaults to off, so existing runs behave as before, and the trajectory appends across restarts. This run sets it to 500 steps through the job's extra LAMMPS arguments.

**Correction to my last message:** the formula I gave was the fluid form. For a solid at fixed strain, stress fluctuations lower the modulus below the affine (Born) value G_B:

G*(ω) = G_B − (V/k_BT)·[C(0) − iω∫C(t)e^(−iωt)dt]

The phonon part of C(t) decays in about 0.1 ps and gives the unrelaxed G_U ≈ 180 GPa. Dislocation glide adds a slow part C_slow, which gives:
- the relaxation strength ΔG = V·C_slow(0)/k_BT and its decay time τ, which together give B and the restoring stiffness k;
- for completely free glide, ΔG → G_U, which would show up as a slow stress noise of about 0.6 GPa rms.

I'll check the stress against the plastic strain from the core separation. The corrected equations are in `results_dislocations/M1_edge001_4000K.md`.

### Claude (11-22 03:46)

I agree that a single constant shift wouldn't matter. These offsets weren't constant, though: they had opposite signs for the two phases and changed with pressure and temperature. Those parts are what change the physics.

**What model 00 showed** (DFT-trained offset, model minus DFT, meV/atom at 300 K):

| state | P0 | P100 | P200 | P300 | P360 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hcp | +35 | +56 | +73 | +80 | +87 |
| fcc | −30 | −40 | −45 | −55 | −50 |

Within each state the scatter was only 1–4 meV/atom, so each phase effectively had its own offset.

**Why each part matters:**
- **hcp and fcc shifted in opposite directions.** On perfect crystals the model gave E(fcc) − E(hcp) = 54 meV/atom; DFT gives 122.6. In hcp Fe a stacking fault, a twin boundary or a dissociated partial dislocation is a few fcc-like layers. Their energies scale roughly with ΔE(fcc−hcp), so the model would have put them at about 45 % of the DFT value. A lower stacking-fault energy also widens the partial-dislocation splitting, which changes core structure and mobility. These are exactly the defects we're adding to the training set for the anelasticity work.
- **The offset changed with volume.** The hcp offset rises 52 meV/atom from V = 10.5 to 6.3 Å³/atom, which is a slope of about 2 GPa in −dE/dV. The model fits the virial separately, so its energy and its stress would not agree with each other along compression.
- **The offset changed with temperature.** The offsets go to about 0 at SIGMA ≥ 0.3 eV (high T). Free-energy differences between temperatures would therefore be wrong, including melting and phase boundaries and the vacancy ΔG_f(T) we planned to use for creep.

So the offsets did show a real problem. The model couldn't distinguish fcc from hcp because the se_e2_a descriptor carries almost no angular information at those sites, and the offsets were a symptom of that. The fix costs little:
- **00t3b** (hybrid se_e2_a + se_e3, 300 K data only) gives ΔE = 124.4 meV/atom, cuts the state offsets to about 5.5 meV/atom rms, and gives lower force errors.
- **00h** (job 7715007, running) applies the same fix to the full training set. Its only cost is training time, about 9× slower.

If you only needed perfect hcp at one P–T, model 00 would have been usable. For defects and stacking-related energetics it wasn't.

### Claude (11-22 04:07)

You're right, "offset" was the wrong word. A shift that changes with structure and volume is an error in E(V, structure, T); a constant shift would have been harmless. Model 00's errors change sign between hcp and fcc and grow with compression (hcp +35 to +87, fcc −30 to −55 meV/atom from P0 to P360), so that's what they were.

I've fixed the wording:
- **Write-up:** `results_Fe/DP_energy_offsets.md` is now `results_Fe/DP_energy_errors.md`. It calls them "state-mean energy errors" and quotes your correction in §1.
- **Tool:** `dp_state_offsets.py` is now `dp_state_errors.py`. I left the old name as a symlink, because the running 00h job (7715007) calls it at the end.
- **INPROGRESS.md:** the current entries use the new wording. The dated history line still says "offsets".

Nothing changes in the diagnosis or the fix. The descriptor couldn't tell fcc from hcp, the hybrid se_e2_a + se_e3 descriptor fixes it, and the 00h retrain is running.
